The area of the square above is increasing. The length of the side of the square is $l.$ Find the rate of change of the area of a square with respect to the length of its side.
after.worked_solution:
The area of the square is given by 

$$
A=A(l)={l}^{2}
$$

where $l$ is the length of the side of the square.

Therefore, the rate of change of $A(l)$ with respect to $l$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{′}(l) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}l}({l}^{2})=2l.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: The bases of a trapezoid are increasing and the larger base is always twice the smaller base. The height of the trapezoid is $2\,cm.$ Find the rate of change of the area of the trapezoid with respect to its smaller base $b.$
after.worked_solution:
The area of a trapezoid is given by 

$$
A=\frac{(B+b)h}{2},
$$

 where $b$ is the smaller base, $B$ is the larger base and $h$ is the height of the trapezoid.

We are given that $B=2b$ and $h=2,$ so we can express the area $A$ as a function of the base $b$ by substituting $B=2b$ and $h=2$ in the formula above. We get

$$
A=\frac{(b+2b)(2)}{2}=3b.
$$

Therefore, the rate of change of $A(b)$ with respect to $b$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{′}(b) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}b}(3b) \\  & =3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}b}(b) \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

after.problem:
The depth $D,$ in meters, of a plant’s root system after $t$ months is modeled by $D(t)=\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{2t+13}.$ What is the instantaneous rate of change of the root depth when $t=6$ months?

The instantaneous rate of change when $t=6$ months is
{{field-1}} meters per month.
after.worked_solution:
The instantaneous rate of change of the root depth when $t=6$ months is equal to ${D}^{′}(6).$ 

First, we take the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{2t+13}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\cdot (2t+13)^{(1/2)-1}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(2t+13)^{-1/2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $t=6,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}^{′}(6) & =\frac{1}{4}(2(6)+13)^{-1/2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4\sqrt{25}} \\  & =\frac{1}{20}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change of the root depth when $t=6$ months is $\frac{1}{20}$ meters per month.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
The surface area $A$ of a cube is increasing. Find the instantaneous rate at which the surface area of the cube is changing with respect to its side length at the moment when the side length of the cube is equal to $3\,\text{in}.$

The instantaneous rate of change at the moment when its side length is $3$ inches is equal to
{{field-1}} ${\text{in}}^{2}/\text{in}.$
after.worked_solution:
We know that the surface area of a cube with side length $s$ is given by 

$$
A=A(s)=6{s}^{2}.
$$

Taking the derivative, the rate of change of $A(s)$ with respect to $s$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{′}(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(6{s}^{2}) \\  & =6(2s) \\  & =12s,\end{aligned}
$$

and evaluating at $s=3$ gives

$$
{A}^{′}(3)=12(3)=36.
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate at which the surface area of the cube is changing when its side length is $3\,\text{in}$, is $36$ ${\text{in}}^{2}/\text{in}.$
